claims.text: Applying an ALD-fabricated nanolaminate of alternating Al2O3 and TiO2 layers will improve the surface physical and mechanical characteristics of high-value metallic components.
Untreated polished metal-alloy surfaces are susceptible to corrosion, wear, and crack propagation under aggressive service conditions.
ALD can produce a controlled nanolaminate composed of alternating Al2O3 and TiO2 layers on the components.
The coating will have a dense, conformal nanolaminate structure.
The nanolaminate will adhere robustly to the metallic substrate.
The nanolaminate will act as a barrier to crack propagation.
The nanolaminate will act as a barrier to chemical attack.
Impeding crack initiation and propagation will enhance the mechanical strength of the coated surface.
Limiting ingress of corrosive species will improve the chemical resistance of the coated surface.
The coating will significantly increase surface hardness relative to an untreated component.
The coating will significantly improve wear resistance relative to an untreated component.
The coating will significantly improve corrosion resistance and reduce corrosion-related weight loss relative to an untreated component.
Adequate substrate preparation is required for the intervention to remain effective.
A coating thickness above a critical minimum, suggested as greater than 10 nm, is required for effectiveness.
Thermal-cycling-induced stresses may degrade coating performance.
The intervention is expected to remain effective in combined high-temperature, corrosive, and high-velocity particulate environments.

The hypothesis is to be rejected if coated specimens fail to show a statistically significant improvement, exemplified by greater than 20% improvements in hardness and wear resistance together with reduced corrosion rates.
